China terms of trade index (base year 2000 = 100), 2010–2020. Explain what is meant by ‘terms of trade’.

questions.questionText: With reference to Figure 1, explain the distinction between direct and indirect taxation.
With reference to the information provided and your own knowledge, assess the likely macroeconomic effects of the German government’s budget deficit.

In Sudan, public services such as healthcare are struggling to keep running. Power outages, blocking of internet access, and fuel shortages, will mean hospitals struggle to operate. Many of the hospitals in the capital city, Khartoum, have reported shortages of doctors, blood, transfusion equipment, medical supplies, and other skilled workers and commodities. Evaluate the possible factors influencing the level of economic development in a developing country of your choice.
Evaluate the microeconomic and macroeconomic effects of a regional trade agreement between the UK and the EU.
Examine two advantages of using the Human Development Index (HDI) to measure the level of economic development in India.
With reference to Extract F, discuss the problems that might be involved with the buffer stock system in India.
Evaluate the microeconomic and macroeconomic reasons for the fall in poverty in India.
Evaluate the microeconomic and macroeconomic effects of rapid increases in population in India.

A group of banks, including Barclays and JP Morgan, have been fined more than €1 billion by the EU’s competition authorities for rigging the foreign exchange market after the Global Financial Crisis of 2008. The EU found that traders at the banks had used online chat rooms to share information about customers’ orders, prices and other trading activities in order to manipulate the currency markets. With reference to the information above, explain what is meant by ‘market rigging’.

A group of banks, including Barclays and JP Morgan, have been fined more than €1 billion by the EU’s competition authorities for rigging the foreign exchange market after the Global Financial Crisis of 2008. The EU found that traders at the banks had used online chat rooms to share information about customers’ orders, prices and other trading activities in order to manipulate the currency markets. Which one of the following is a role of financial markets? To:
options: discourage saving
promote moral hazard
provide forward markets
restrict free trade

questions.questionText: In March 2018 the US imposed a tariff of 25% on steel imports from the UK. Explain the likely impact of this tariff on the steel market in the US.
In March 2018 the US imposed a tariff of 25% on steel imports from the UK. Which one of the following is likely to give the US a comparative advantage in steel production? An increase in:
options: corporation tax in the US
economic growth in the US
the productivity of US steel workers
the wages of US steel workers

questions.questionText: The table below shows the UK’s budget deficit between March 2016 and March 2019. Which one of the following will most likely lead to a reduction in the budget deficit?
options: An increase in government spending and a decrease in taxation
An increase in taxation and a decrease in government spending
An increase in the value of exports and a decrease in the value of imports
An increase in the value of imports and a decrease in the value of exports

questions.questionText: With reference to Figure 4 and your own knowledge, explain the distinction between a progressive and a regressive tax.
With reference to Figure 4 and Extract A, examine the likely impact of the ‘freeze in income tax thresholds’ (Extract A line 1) on aggregate demand.
Assess whether a fiscal deficit and national debt should be a cause for concern for the UK government.
With reference to Extract B, discuss the use of quantitative easing in preventing deflation.

In 2021 Brazil’s current account deficit on the balance of payments was US$46.12 billion. The Central Bank of Brazil intervened to sell its own currency, the real, on September 23rd 2022. This was the first time it has intervened in foreign currency markets since December 2021. Evaluate macroeconomic policies that could be used to reduce a current account deficit. Refer to a country of your choice in your answer.
In 2020, exports as a share of world GDP were 12% higher than in 2000, almost twice as high as 50 years ago. Evaluate the possible factors contributing to globalisation.
Evaluate the microeconomic and macroeconomic advantages for a country specialising in energy production using gas.
Explain one reason why a country might operate a managed exchange rate. Refer to Extract D in your answer.
With reference to the second paragraph of Extract E, examine two likely problems for the expansion of the chocolate industry in Ghana.
Evaluate the microeconomic and macroeconomic effects of high interest rates in Ghana, or another developing country of your choice.
Evaluate the microeconomic and macroeconomic effects of Ghana joining the African Continental Free Trade Agreement (Extract F).
In 2021, the US total GDP was $23 trillion and national debt was $28.4 trillion. Calculate the US national debt in 2021 as a percentage of GDP.
In 2021, the US total GDP was $23 trillion and national debt was $28.4 trillion. Explain the relationship between a fiscal deficit and the national debt.
In 2021, the US total GDP was $23 trillion and national debt was $28.4 trillion. Which one of the following is the most likely consequence of an increase in the US national debt? An increase in:
options: crowding out
inequality
poverty
unemployment

questions.questionText: With reference to Extract A, explain what is meant by a ‘regional trade agreement’ (Extract A, line 7).
With reference to Extract A, examine two causes of the high cost of transporting goods between African countries.
Discuss the impact of improved transport links between African countries on economic growth rates.
Assess two likely benefits of debt relief to Angola. Refer to Extract B in your answer.
Discuss market-orientated strategies the Angolan government could use to improve development.

In 2022 the value of UK exports fell by 14% compared with 2020. In contrast, the global average increase in exports was 8.2% over the same time period. The UK’s competitiveness also fell, dropping five places from 18th in 2021 to 23rd in 2022 in the world competitiveness rankings. Evaluate macroeconomic policies that could be used to increase international competitiveness in the UK’s export markets.
Evaluate microeconomic and macroeconomic policies that could be used to reduce inequality in the UK.
Evaluate the likely microeconomic and macroeconomic effects of tax cuts in the UK.
Using the data provided in Extract D, explain one role of financial markets.
Evaluate the microeconomic and macroeconomic effects of falling house prices.
Bank of England base interest rate, 2016–2020 Which one of the following would be most likely to result from lower base interest rates? A fall in:
options: the average price of houses
the external value of the pound
the level of employment
the rate of economic growth

In May 2020, the UK government introduced a loan scheme to help small businesses survive the downturn in the economy. Small businesses could borrow up to £50 000 at an interest rate of 2.5% for up to 6 years from a bank. The government guaranteed 100% of the loans, to enable banks to issue them quickly, and only minimal checks were made on borrowers. With reference to the information above, explain one role of financial markets.

In May 2020, the UK government introduced a loan scheme to help small businesses survive the downturn in the economy. Small businesses could borrow up to £50 000 at an interest rate of 2.5% for up to 6 years from a bank. The government guaranteed 100% of the loans, to enable banks to issue them quickly, and only minimal checks were made on borrowers. Which one of the following would be a risk if ‘only minimal checks were made on borrowers’ in this loan scheme?
options: Asymmetric information
Crowding out
Market rigging
Speculation

questions.questionText: Using a Lorenz curve diagram, explain how income inequality is measured using the Gini coefficient. Refer to Extract A in your answer.
With reference to Figure 1 and Extract A, examine two likely causes of income inequality within the UK.
With reference to Extract C and your own knowledge, discuss methods the UK government could use to increase tax revenue.

Both China and the United States have been gradually increasing the tariffs imposed on each other’s exports as their trade dispute continues. The IMF estimated that the trade dispute between China and the United States would reduce global GDP growth by 0.8 percentage points by the end of 2020. Evaluate the likely impact of an increase in protectionism on the global economy.

With global economic growth slowing and inequality rising, the case against globalisation is strengthening. But there are also many benefits to globalisation. Global trade and international trade agreements allow countries to focus on their strengths and share expertise, as well as reducing risk through diversification. Evaluate the likely impact of globalisation on the global economy.
Evaluate the microeconomic and macroeconomic effects of a depreciation of the pound. Refer to restaurants or other food delivery services in your answer.
Explain what is meant by the Lewis model. Refer to Extract D in your answer.
Examine two demographic factors influencing development in Kenya.
Using the example of cut flowers (Extract F), discuss how the concept of absolute advantage may lead to growth in Kenya. Use numerical or diagrammatic analysis in your answer.
Evaluate the microeconomic and macroeconomic effects of decreasing interest rates in Kenya, or another developing country of your choice.
Evaluate the microeconomic and macroeconomic strategies that could be used to promote development in Kenya, or another developing country of your choice.

After the Global Financial Crisis of 2008, the US President introduced expansionary fiscal policies of $800 billion. The International Monetary Fund estimated that the multiplier at the time was approximately 1.5. Explain the impact of annual fiscal deficits on the US national debt.

British pound to US dollar exchange rate (value of one pound in dollars), June 2017 to June 2019. Which one of the following has been the overall change in the British pound to US dollar exchange rate from 1st January 2018 to 1st January 2019?
options: Appreciation
Depreciation
Devaluation
Revaluation

questions.questionText: British pound to US dollar exchange rate (value of one pound in dollars), June 2017 to June 2019. Explain the likely impact of the change in the exchange rate of the pound shown in the graph from 1st January 2018 to 1st January 2019 on the UK current account of the balance of payments.

A number of business groups have signed an open letter to the UK Government asking it to commit to delivering the full High Speed 2 rail link. This will connect London to the northern cities of Manchester and Leeds at a cost of £56 billion and reduce journey times by as much as 50%. Government spending on the High Speed 2 rail link is an example of which of the following?
options: Automatic stabilisers
Capital expenditure
Current expenditure
Transfer payments

questions.questionText: Using the data in Figures 1 and 2, calculate the change in the level of total aid funding to Rwanda between 2011 and 2012.
With reference to the information provided, examine two likely benefits for the Rwandan economy of the growth in the country’s population.
With reference to the information provided, assess the likely impact on the Rwandan economy of the change in aid received between 2017 and 2018.
Discuss the likely impact on Rwandan consumers and clothing manufacturers of the increase in the tariff on imports of second-hand clothes. Use an appropriate diagram to support your answer.
Discuss policies, other than import tariffs, that the Rwandan government could use to develop its manufacturing industries.

The European Central Bank introduced a new round of quantitative easing (QE) in March 2020, purchasing up to €750 billion of assets. The objective of this QE was to reduce the serious risks to the effectiveness of monetary policy resulting from a significant recession. The European Central Bank’s target for inflation remains at ‘below but close to 2%’. Evaluate the effectiveness of quantitative easing during ‘a significant recession’.
Explain one reason why a country such as Germany wants to avoid an increase in the national debt relative to GDP (Figure 2).

In 2018, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) lent Argentina $57 billion as part of a bailout package to help prevent the country’s government defaulting on its debts. This financial crisis also caused significant capital flight out of Argentina’s economy. Explain the role of the IMF in providing financial assistance to countries such as Argentina.

The UK’s net monthly balance of trade in goods and services, by value, January 2014 to January 2018, is shown in the chart below. Which one of the following can be inferred from the above chart over the period shown?
options: The government was spending more than it received in taxation
The UK’s balance of trade, by value, was always in equilibrium
The value of imports was greater than the value of exports
The value of inflows was greater than the value of outflows

questions.questionText: In 2018, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) lent Argentina $57 billion as part of a bailout package to help prevent the country’s government defaulting on its debts. This financial crisis also caused significant capital flight out of Argentina’s economy. Which one of the following is most likely to happen to Argentina’s currency value as a result of capital flight, assuming it is operating with a floating exchange rate system?
options: Appreciation
Depreciation
Devaluation
Revaluation

questions.questionText: With reference to Figure 1 and Extract A, explain the likely impact of a Fairtrade scheme on agricultural communities.
Examine two ways, apart from Fairtrade schemes, in which cocoa farmers could boost their incomes despite the falling price of cocoa.
Discuss the problems for the Ivory Coast of dependency on cocoa for a large proportion of their exports. Refer to Figure 2 in your answer.

Nigeria is considering joining the African Continental Free Trade Agreement. Assess policies the Nigerian government could use in response to the concerns of the country’s ‘manufacturers and trade unions’ (Extract B paragraph 3) if they join this trading bloc.
Discuss the likely benefits of increased economic integration for sub‑Saharan African countries.

In 2018, the United States Government cut the corporation tax rate (tax on company profits) from 35% to 21%. Income tax rates for US citizens were also reduced: for example, the top rate of income tax was cut from 39.6% to 37%. Evaluate the likely impact of cutting tax rates as a policy to increase economic growth.

In terms of income distribution and wealth distribution Brazil is one of the most unequal countries in the world. Its income Gini coefficient is 0.449 and it is ranked number 2 in the world for its wealth inequality. Evaluate possible economic causes of income and wealth inequalities within a country such as Brazil.
Explain how the Turkish central bank intervenes in the currency market to prevent ‘excessive appreciation or depreciation of the Turkish lira’ (Extract A, lines 7–8).
Examine two reasons why the Turkish government may want to avoid a significant fall in the exchange rate of the Turkish lira.
Apart from literacy and numeracy skills in young workers, examine one reason for the trend in productivity in the UK, over the period shown in Figure 4.
Evaluate possible microeconomic and macroeconomic policies which could be used to improve UK competitiveness.

The International Monetary Fund has called on the G20 group of large industrialised countries to boost government spending on infrastructure. Which one of the following would be an example of government spending on infrastructure? An increase in:
options: construction work on new railway lines
interest payments on the national debt
salaries for teachers
unemployment benefit payments

The UK Government is planning to cut the rate of corporation tax on all pre-tax profits of companies to 17% by 2020. Explain one possible reason why the revenue from corporation tax could increase if the government cuts the rate of tax.
